# Peter K Dunn's Educational Resources

> Comprehensive textbooks on scientific research methodology and statistical distribution theory for quantitative research.

Peter K Dunn maintains two interconnected textbooks covering the foundations of scientific research design, statistical methods, and probability theory. The materials are built with R, bookdown, and Markdown to provide interactive, reproducible learning resources for students and researchers.

## Key Topics

- Scientific Research and Methodology
- hypothesis testing
- probability theory
- quantitative research
- research design
- statistical distributions
- research methodology
- scientific method
- evidence-based research
- random procedures
- sample spaces
- correlation and regression
- research questions
- R programming
- beginner-friendly education

## Scientific Research and Methodology Textbook

- [Preface | Scientific Research and Methodology](https://peterkdunn.github.io/SRM-Textbook/): Textbook preface on quantitative research design, hypothesis testing, and statistics
- [1 Research: an introduction | Scientific Research and Methodology](https://peterkdunn.github.io/SRM-Textbook/Intro.html): Introduction to quantitative and qualitative research methods and scientific process
- [2 Research questions | Scientific Research and Methodology](https://peterkdunn.github.io/SRM-Textbook/RQs.html): Guide to formulating quantitative research questions and identifying variables
- [18 Probability | Scientific Research and Methodology](https://peterkdunn.github.io/SRM-Textbook/Probability.html): Guide to probability theory and random sample statistics in research methodology
- [33 Correlation and regression: CIs and tests | Scientific Research and Methodology](https://peterkdunn.github.io/SRM-Textbook/CorrelationRegression.html): Statistical methods for correlation analysis, regression, and hypothesis testing

## Statistical Distribution Theory

- [Preface | The Theory of Statistical Distributions](https://peterkdunn.github.io/DistTheory/): Textbook introduction to mathematical statistics and statistical distribution theory
